summaries.summary: Task-oriented dialogue systems use manually engineered task-specific ontologies with slots and values as semantic representations in modular and end-to-end systems.
Explicit semantics create challenges including scarce annotated domain-specific data, constrained dialogue types, and expensive in-domain data collection for new domains.
The paper presents PolyResponse, a non-generative response retrieval conversational search engine trained on hundreds of millions of Reddit conversations for restaurant search and booking.
The demo focuses on PolyResponse's practical restaurant search usefulness, multi-modal extension, booking assistance, and retrieval-based avoidance of ontology, generation, and policy modules.
PolyResponse combines text responses with visual information, supports voice input and visual output, and is deployed in 8 languages for restaurants in 8 cities.
PolyResponse is a ranking model scoring replies and photos in conversational context using scaled cosine similarities S(r,c) and S(p,c).
The text model trains on hundreds of millions context-reply (c,r) pairs using lower-cased tokenised unigrams and bigrams with wildcard replacements and a Reddit-based vocabulary.
Training learns d=320 shared features, transformer-based 320-dimensional encodings, three 1,024-dimensional hidden layers, and final l=512 representations h_c and h_r.
Training constrains C between 0 and sqrt(l), maximises context-reply similarity, minimises random pairings, and uses SGD batches of 500 pairs with 1 positive and 499 negatives.
Photos use ImageNet-pretrained CNN models, specifically MobileNet with depth multiplier 1.4 and 224 x 224 input, producing a 1,792-dimensional representation mapped to h_p.
The Reddit dataset spans January 2015 to December 2018 and almost 3.7B comments, yielding more than 727M context-reply (c,r) pairs after preprocessing.
A photo encoder is learned on pretrained MobileNet CNN using around 200K Yelp Open dataset photos and captions to maximise caption-photo similarity.
At inference, the Yelp dataset supplies city-limited candidates; English Edinburgh uses 396 restaurants, 4,225 photos, 6,725 responses, and 125,830 review sentences.
PolyResponse jointly trains f(context) and g(reply) on Reddit, freezes g(), learns t(photo) on Yelp, and retrieves plausible text replies and photo responses.
Inference computes h_c and finds nearby h_r and h_p vectors, with pre-computed response vectors and optimised nearest neighbour search scaling to billions of candidates.
PolyResponse offers voice and text input and output, with Google Cloud tools supporting speech-to-text and text-to-speech conversion.
Restaurant-browsing dialogue flow represents state as a monotonically decreasing set of relevant restaurants, where valid restaurants have relevant responses to new user input.
S1 initialises R as all restaurants in the city and ranks all responses in the response pool pertaining to restaurants in R.
S2 retrieves the top N responses r_1, r_2, ..., r_N with sorted cosine similarity scores s_1 >= s_2 >= ... >= s_N.
S3 computes probability scores p_i proportional to exp(a * s_i) with sum from i=1 to N of p_i, where a>0 is tunable.
S4 computes q_e for each restaurant/entity e in R as q_e = sum over i: r_i in e of p_i.
S5 updates R to the smallest set of restaurants with highest q whose q-values sum to more than predefined threshold t.
S6 displays the most relevant responses associated with the updated R and returns to S2.

The system displays responses from multiple relevant restaurants or top N responses and photos for one restaurant, using internal narrowing and templatic spoken rules without dedicated modules or explicit task-tailored semantics.
Intent classifiers can reset the dialogue state or activate the separate restaurant booking dialogue flow.
PolyResponse restaurant search is available in 8 languages for 8 cities, using a Google Translate translate-to-source approach for foreign language responses and user utterances.
Voice-controlled menu search ranks available menu items and retrieves those semantically relevant to the current user utterance using the same methodology as other responses.
Two binary intent classifiers using h_c, a single-layer neural net with ReLU and 100 hidden nodes, and sets of 20 paraphrases support resetting R and switching to slot-based booking.

The paper presents search-based dialogue without explicit semantic representations, allowing multi-modal responses, with future work on more tasks, languages, encoders, ranking functions, and complex flows.
